tasks.spec:
You are a repo feature worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repository, detached at HEAD. Edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP: you own exactly two paths, scripts/tg_approval.py (existing) and tests/test_tg_approval.py (existing). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else under scripts/, tests/, or server/. Do NOT git commit, do NOT git push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave your changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT AND STAKES. scripts/tg_approval.py is deployed to a live VPS and drives two different phone workflows through Telegram inline buttons.
  --kind card is the EMAIL SEND-APPROVAL lane. Its Approve button posts 'APPROVE external_send' on a Linear card, and a separate deterministic executor then actually sends a real email to a real person. This lane is LIVE and you must not change its behaviour in any way.
  --kind escalation is the loop-escalation lane. Today it offers 'Ack' and 'Respond'. The owner has decided (2026-08-05) to remove Acknowledge entirely: every tap must be a decision, either approved as-is or a written response. That is what you are changing.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY: scripts/tg_approval.py in full, especially cmd_prompt, build_comment, build_fix_notes_comment, parse_callback and handle_callback; and tests/test_tg_approval.py for the existing test style.

CHANGE 1, REFACTOR FOR TESTABILITY. cmd_prompt currently builds the prompt text and the inline keyboard inline and then calls Telegram. Extract that into a PURE function that touches no network:
    build_prompt(kind, card, to, subject, preview, nonce, action_class='proposal', reescalation=0, first_raised='') -> (text, keyboard)
Accept those as keyword arguments. cmd_prompt must then call build_prompt and send the result, so its behaviour is unchanged but now verifiable offline. Keep the existing 'Open card in Linear' url button row exactly as it is.

CHANGE 2, THE ESCALATION BUTTONS. For kind 'escalation' the action row becomes exactly TWO buttons:
  a button whose text reads as Approve (an emoji is fine) carrying callback action 'a'
  a button whose text reads as Respond (an emoji is fine) carrying callback action 'f'
The word Ack must not appear. Update the YOUR MOVE lines to match: Approve means approved as-is and is recorded on the card; Respond means reply to this message and your words land on the card, and is also how you decline or ask for something different. Callback data keeps its existing 'v1|<action>|<card>|<nonce>' shape.

CHANGE 3, THE ACTION CLASS. build_comment currently hardcodes the module constant ACTION_CLASS ('external_send') for an approve. Give it an action_class keyword whose DEFAULT is 'proposal', and thread it from build_prompt. This matters more than it looks: 'APPROVE external_send' is a real send authorization that a separate executor consumes. A loop escalation must never emit it by accident. An explicitly passed action_class must still be honoured so the email lane is unaffected. build_comment must keep working when called with its original three positional arguments.

CHANGE 4, THE RE-ESCALATION HEADER. build_prompt takes reescalation (an integer, default 0) and first_raised (an ISO date string, default empty). When reescalation is greater than 0 the prompt text must say it is a re-escalation, show the count, and show the first_raised date, so the owner can tell an old unanswered item from a new one at a glance. When reescalation is 0 the text must NOT claim to be a re-escalation.

DO NOT CHANGE: the --kind card action row (three buttons, callback actions a, f, s in that order), the nonce lifecycle, owner-id checks, state file handling, the consumer loop, or the force-reply path that turns an owner's typed reply into a FIX-NOTES comment.

UPDATE tests/test_tg_approval.py with cases for the new behaviour, including one that pins the --kind card action row so a future change cannot silently move the email send lane. Your tests are not the acceptance gate; an independent oracle drives build_prompt and build_comment through assertions you have not seen.

VERIFY before you finish, from the worktree root:
  PLACEHOLDER_MODE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_tg_approval.py tests/test_obe_tg_notify.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
PLACEHOLDER_MODE=1 is required: it is the guard that keeps a test run from buzzing a real person's phone. Never run these tests without it.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave the two owned files edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree (the check copies it out before the worktree is deleted) recording what you read, what you changed, what you deliberately did not change and why, the exact verification command and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no network, no Telegram call, no Linear call, no real send. No new dependencies. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service. If something is ambiguous, state the assumption in ./notes.md rather than widening your ownership.
tasks.verified: an independent oracle imported the refactored module and asserted offline that --kind escalation now offers exactly Approve (callback 'a') and Respond (callback 'f') with no Ack, that --kind card still offers its original three buttons with actions a/f/s so the live email send lane did not move, that an approve defaults to the inert 'APPROVE proposal' and never to external_send while still honouring an explicit action class, and that a re-escalated prompt announces itself with count and first-raised date while a first prompt does not; the podcast tg test suite passed under PLACEHOLDER_MODE=1; only owned files changed; and the patch was exported outside the worktree.
